why: Same discharge-for-suppression principle; probationary status and notice are not addressed in the passage.

span: Whether the Labour Court at Delhi had jurisdiction to try the complaint/case of appellant- workman
why: Territorial jurisdiction of a Labour Court; not about termination procedure.

span: Of a workman on probation by giving 7 days notice by giving 24 hours notice in writing or wages/stipend in lieu of notice
why: Reproduces a Standing Order requiring notice (or wages in lieu) for terminating a probationary workman; it is quoted rule text, not the court's holding.

span: An employer is entitled to satisfy itself as to the competence of a probationer to be confirmed in service
why: Quoted from an earlier decision on non-punitive termination of a probationer after an enquiry; says nothing about prior notice and adoption is not shown.

span: the employee was required to be paid one month salary in lieu of notice
why: Termination with pay in lieu of notice under an appointment letter; the employee is not shown to be a probationer.

span: including the potential for termination without prior notice
why: Learned ASG's submission about temporary (explicitly not probationary) employees; a party argument, different condition.

span: seven days notice with respect to workman who is on probation and temporary workman by serving a 24 hours notice
why: Court describes the Standing Order notice periods while deciding a resignation question; does not itself rule on terminating probationers without notice.

span: the services of an employee may be terminated without notice during the period of probation
why: Quoted text of Rule 105 stating the proposition for that school; the passage reproduces the rule, the court's holding concerns deemed confirmation.

span: the employer is under an obligation to comply with the twin conditions of Section 25F of the Act 1947 before the retrenchment is given effect to
why: General s.25F rule for workmen with 240 days; whether a probationer is covered or excepted is not stated.

span: his services cannot be terminated in the usual manner of the other regular employees of the Institute but are terminable on either side by notice
why: Decides whether a doctor is an employee or independent professional for an insurance exclusion.

span: Order of termination passed against the appellant is arbitrary, illegal and in violation of the principles of natural justice
why: Termination of a permanent employee after 26 years on a police report; not a probationer.

span: the continuation of the services of a probationer beyond the maximum period of probation would amount to a deemed confirmation of service only in the absence of a stipulation
why: Concerns deemed confirmation of probationers, not whether termination needs notice.

span: it was a case of the employee abandoning his services without informing his employer about his whereabouts
why: Abandonment of service and service of notices to an absent employee; not probation.
